revision: P1D.1a - separates observed selection analysis from held-out design attribution; corrects 44-imperfect accounting; replaces causal claims with slice-informed hypotheses; corrects saturation arithmetic and wording per external review
authority: P1D.1 - draft for user review. NOT frozen. No gate closed.
critical_separation_invariant: observed_selection44 and case_design_all66 are reported SEPARATELY and never combined. The v1 '4/44 imperfect' aggregate is retracted: 2 of those 4 SEMANTIC_GENERALIZATION cases are held-out with no observed metrics.

saturation_arithmetic_corrected.claim_retracted: v1 said the gate was 'arithmetically impossible' / the benchmark was at 'ceiling'. This was too strong.

correct_arithmetic.max_gain_interpretation: A candidate that scored perfectly on all 22 non-ceiling cases could reach at most +0.0505 macro. The +0.03 gate is therefore NOT arithmetically impossible.
correct_arithmetic.correct_wording: The benchmark is PARTIALLY saturated and gives the frozen macro gate limited power to detect improvements concentrated in a subset of workflows. A +0.03 gain remains mathematically possible but requires an average +0.06 improvement across the non-ceiling half without regression on the ceiling half.

observed_failure_distribution_selection4.description: OBSERVED behavior on the 44 selection cases ONLY. Held-out is excluded (no per-policy metrics).
observed_failure_distribution_selection4.important_caveat: For non-ceiling cases, the OBSERVED fact is that lexical is imperfect. The CAUSE is not measured per-case; slice_expected_failure_mode is a DESIGN HYPOTHESIS, not a measured diagnosis. 'Semantic generalization' here means 'the slice was designed to test semantic generalization AND lexical was observed imperfect on it' - it does NOT prove the imperfection was caused by a representation deficit.

case_design_distribution_all66.description: CASE-DESIGN attribution for ALL 66 cases, by slice_expected_failure_mode. This is a design prior (what each slice was built to exercise), NOT an observed measurement of cause. Held-out cases appear here by design; their observed behavior is unknown.

embedding_relevance_signal_SOFTENED.v1_claim_retracted: v1 said the other 91% of imperfect cases were 'failures none of which a larger embedding addresses'. This was too strong: a better embedding COULD affect ranking or agenda discrimination.
embedding_relevance_signal_SOFTENED.correct_claim: The current evidence establishes only that the non-SEMANTIC_GENERALIZATION categories do not, BY THEMSELVES, establish an embedding-capacity deficit. They do not rule out that an embedding could help indirectly (e.g., via ranking or agenda discrimination). The honest reading: the historical data does not isolate embedding capacity as the DOMINANT bottleneck, but does not exonerate it either.
